deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the previous page. Let π̂ be the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}, with inertia generators l_0, l_1, l_∞ satisfying l_∞ l_1 l_0 = 1. Grothendieck considers outer automorphisms u in a group Σ̂^! (inside Autext^!(π̂,(l_i))). Each such u sends every l_i to a conjugate of a power: u(l_i) = int(g_i) l_i^p, with p ∈ Ẑ^* (the cyclotomic-type character). The conjugators g_i are determined only up to right multiplication by powers of l_i.

The group SΣ̂^!. It consists of tuples (p, g_0, g_1, g_∞) ∈ Ẑ^* × π̂^{0,1,∞} satisfying relation (22). It is an extension of Σ̂^! by Ẑ^{0,1,∞}. The maps γ_i : (u,(g_i)) ↦ g_i form a 1-cocycle on SΣ̂^! with values in π̂^{0,1,∞}. The kernel of SΣ̂^! → Autext^!(π̂,(l_i)) is identified with π̂ × Ẑ^{0,1,∞}.

This page.
- The first line completes that identification. To (g,(d_i)) one associates the system with p = 1 and g_i = g·l_i^{d_i}. So inner automorphisms by g, together with the free choice of powers of l_i in the conjugators, give exactly the kernel.
- Next comes a programme note. One should make explicit the operations σ_i (and ε_i) of the S_3 = 𝔖_{0,1,∞} symmetry group on the extended group SΣ̃^! and on its elements ũ, acting by conjugation.
- One identity is stated: the σ_i are covariant under the order-3 rotation ρ, i.e. σ_i(ρ ũ ρ^{-1}) = σ_{i+1}(ũ). This is the cyclic relabelling 0→1→∞.
- The oblique margin note proposes a parallel discrete version: an extension SΣ of the discrete group Σ by Z^{0,1,∞}. It mentions conjugations and lifting elements σ_i ρ to the extension.

Purpose. The next page (numbered 12, a new draft) treats the extension 𝓔_{0,3} of Γ_{0,3} ≅ 𝔖_3 × Z/2 by Π_{0,3}, and its classes of maximal partial splittings attached to fixed points of ρ and σ_i. So this page prepares for 'rigidifying' the automorphisms of π̂_{0,3}: lifting outer automorphisms to genuine automorphisms with chosen conjugators (tangential-basepoint data) compatible with the S_3 symmetries. This is the germ of what became the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group (cocycle f, 2-cycle and 3-cycle/hexagon relations), here only sketched.
errors: No mathematical error is visible; the page is a fragment.
The symbol rendered 'δΣ̃' is Grothendieck's 'SΣ̃' (the extended group S Σ̂^! of the previous page).
The covariance formula is stated without checking compatibility of the chosen conjugators g_i with ρ. That check is not carried out.

missed.claim: Grothendieck plans to make explicit the S_3-action on the rigidified extension SΣ̂^! (cocycle γ_i with values in π̂^3) and its covariance under ρ. This is a pre-Drinfeld attempt at the symmetry relations defining GT̂. It is abandoned here; the next page restarts the topic via splittings of 𝓔_{0,3}.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents historically that Grothendieck in 1981 was working with the 1-cocycle/three-conjugator formalism and S_3-equivariance that later yield GT̂. The mathematics itself is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a short, partly crossed-out programmatic fragment. The ideas (three conjugators, cocycle, S_3 covariance) are precursors of GT̂, known to exist in Grothendieck's 1981 work. No new result is stated.
